text: Twenty pages from the old vet become a short summary and the right reminders. But a computer wrote the draft, so a person checks it before it goes on the chart.
The one thing to remember: Scout drafts the summary and reminders, but nothing goes in the record until a person checks them and clicks Enter.
File the document on the request.
It's on Biscuit's chart now, and the request moves to Received.
Open Received, then Review and summarize.
Give the document a clear name, like the hospital and what it is. Then save names and summarize.
Scout reads the document. It takes a few seconds.
The draft is ready. The document is beside it.
Scout found what's due, with when it was last done. Check each date against the record, and fix any that are wrong.
Read the summary. Edit anything that's wrong, and make sure warnings, like a pet that snaps at exams, made it in.
Then enter them in the record.
Scout says exactly what it will add, including that the family sees the reminders in their portal. Confirm.

The most common mistakes: entering the reminders without checking the dates, and missing a behavior warning in the summary. Remember: Scout drafts it, a person checks it, and nothing goes in the record until you click Enter.
